messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion for the latest chat-check branch shows weird behavior: first token of generated chat responses is sometimes "<|pad|>" instead of the expected system/bos text. break in chatfmt tests and a small but consistent drop in our convo-eval scores.

sam: oof. which model + tokenizer? any diffs in config.json or added_tokens.json after conversion?

maya: model: local/mistral-chat-lite-v2-exported. Tokenizer was huggingface fast tokenizer, we ran the conversion script (hf_to_redwood.py) and then our onboarder. I inspected the files:

jen: can you paste tokenizer.special_tokens_map and pad/bos ids?

maya: pasted below from the converted assets:
```
special_tokens_map: {"bos_token": "<|bos|>", "eos_token": "<|eos|>"}
config.json: {"bos_token_id": 0, "eos_token_id": 2, "pad_token_id": 1}
added_tokens.json: ["<|pad|>", "<|system|>"]
```

sam: that ordering is suspicious — added_tokens.json puts <|pad|> first so new token got id 1 (because the base vocab reserved 0 for BOS), but config.json still says pad_token_id:1 while the model's initial int mappings expect pad=0 in some spots?

arjun: quick note: some of our quantized runtime paths assume pad_token_id==0 for masked KV allocation. If pad got remapped to 1 during the HF added_tokens injection, the runtime doesn't zero-out cache rows correctly -> early-token spurious output.

jen: can you run this quick repro to confirm the tokenizer mapping? paste output of: 
```
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/mistral-chat-lite-v2-exported')
print('pad', t.pad_token, t.pad_token_id)
print('bos', t.bos_token, t.bos_token_id)
print('convert ids', t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|pad|>','<|bos|>','<|system|>']))
PY
```

maya: output: `pad <|pad|> 1, bos <|bos|> 0, convert ids [1,0,2]`

sam: so HF tokenizer assigned pad=1, bos=0. Why does config.json show pad_token_id:1 and model internals/our runtime sometimes expect different? Where's the drift happening?

arjun: common cause: there are two sources of truth — config.json (from model repo) and tokenizer files (added_tokens.json + merges/vocab). During our hf_to_redwood step we were merging added_tokens after the conversion in a deterministic order that differs from HF fast-tokenizer's internal build order. If the on-disk order changes, IDs shift.

maya: i think we did: load tokenizer -> save_pretrained -> run redwood_consolidate which concatenates added_tokens upstream. That can reorder new tokens.

jen: short-term mitigation: after conversion, force special tokens mapping to explicit ids in the tokenizer config before save_pretrained, e.g., set tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(expected_pad_id) or set special_tokens_map and pad_token_id explicitly.

sam: agreed. Also add a validation check in hf_to_redwood: assert tokenizer.pad_token_id == int(config['pad_token_id']) and same for bos/eos. Fail the conversion if mismatch.

maya: i ran a small test: with the explicit fix (set tokenizer.pad_token = '<|pad|>'; tokenizer._convert_special_tokens_to_ids()), the chatfmt tests pass locally and quantized run no longer shows early pad characters.

jen: can we also detect when added_tokens.json contains tokens that match conventional special tokens (<|pad|>, <|bos|>, <|eos|>, <|unk|>) and prefer to treat them as "special" rather than as added vocabulary? That would help avoid id-shift in many HF imports.

arjun: good idea. Implementation note: treat any added tokens whose string matches the known special token set as a remap candidate; remove from added_tokens.json and inject into special_tokens_map with the existing token id if present, otherwise append to the end and update config.json. Also add a golden test that loads the converted tokenizer then runs a small convo generation to assert first token != pad.

maya: filing a follow-up PR: 
- fail conversion on special token id mismatch
- auto-promote known special tokens from added_tokens.json into special_tokens_map
- unit test with quantized runtime that checks KV allocation when pad_token_id != 0

modelbot: deploy-checker: new commit queued for branch hf-to-redwood/special-token-fix, CI: unit tests + chatfmt-eval. :eyes:

sam: thanks — once PR lands i'll re-run the 12-model quantization sweep to see if any other models have similar drift.

maya: thanks all. leaving logs & quick repro in the conversion PR.
